exclude_overhire.note: Overhire, day-call and show-by-show crew work is EXCLUDED by default — it is not a career move and it drowns the inventory. THE EXCEPTION (Michael, 2026-09-10): if the work is within `home_base.accessible_radius_miles`, it QUALIFIES and gets rowed. Reasoning: near home, show-by-show work costs no relocation, needs no notice, and is availability income Michael can actually take. Far from home the same posting is noise. Rate is NOT the test and there is no floor on this exception — Michael, on SM work, 2026-09-02: 'open to far less esp if it's nearby.' Mark these rows `level=contract` and set `accessibility=home` so they can be filtered out of career-arc reporting without being hidden from the sweep.

home_base.note: Home base, and NOT a preference — geography stays 'anywhere' and relocation stays live. This block exists only to define what 'immediately accessible' MEANS so the overhire exception and the accessibility tiers are testable rather than vibes. 90 miles is a commutable same-day round trip and it deliberately reaches Syracuse (~87mi) and Buffalo (~75mi), which are the two nearest markets with real producing houses. ⚠ Ask Michael before widening this; do not quietly grow it to make a find qualify.

highlight_tiers.note: Added 2026-09-10 by Michael's ruling. These are REPORTING tiers, not filters — nothing is excluded for lacking a tier, and a row can hold more than one. Ricky tags rows; Corso surfaces them. Purpose: remote and near-home work is immediately actionable in a way a relocation-required role is not, and the standing inventory had no way to say so. ✅ Carried into the state files as the `accessibility` column on 2026-09-18; tags are pipe-separated when a row holds more than one.

tiers.remote: Posting explicitly states remote or fully-distributed. Never inferred from a job title — if the posting does not say it, the row does not get the tag. ⚠ Quote the words. A board's metadata card reading '(Remote)' over a body reading 'Work Location: In-office' is a live case from 2026-09-18 — the BODY wins and the tag is refused. Two more the same day advertised 'Remote' on a board card while the employer feed said Kansas City and Denver. ⚠ AND remote rarely means location-free: capture required states, travel and in-person obligations in the `location` field. 🔴 2026-09-27: a CONDITIONAL remote arrangement is HYBRID, not remote. 'Fridays may be remote with supervisor approval' and 'option to be fully remote' are hybrid. Five rows were self-corrected from remote to hybrid on that basis in one pass; 'fully remote' or '100% remote' is the bar for the remote tag.
tiers.hybrid: Posting explicitly states hybrid or partial-remote, with a named onsite anchor. Same never-inferred rule as remote.
tiers.home: Within `home_base.accessible_radius_miles`. No relocation, no notice period. This is the ONE tier that may be derived rather than quoted, because it is arithmetic on a stated location.
tiers.immediate: Start date is now/ASAP/open-until-filled AND applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no deadline gate. This is about SPEED TO WORK, which is a different question from geography — keep the two tags separate and never collapse them.
tiers.⚠_platform_structural: OPEN QUESTION, raised 2026-09-26, not yet ruled by Michael. A freelance marketplace (Upwork, Cad Crowd) is remote BY THE NATURE OF THE PLATFORM, but the individual listing body often never says the word. Six rows in the 09-26 pass were tagged `remote` on platform structure rather than a body quote and were marked as such in the row text. Does platform structure satisfy the never-infer rule, or must the body say it? Until ruled: tag it, but write 'platform-structural — NOT a body quote' into the row so it is never mistaken for quoted evidence.

highlight_tiers.reporting: The pass summary carries a ⚡ ACCESSIBLE block listing every row tagged remote / hybrid / home / immediate, sitting alongside ⚡ Spotlight. If the block is EMPTY, say so explicitly and say which sources were swept for it — an absent block and a swept-empty one are different facts, and conflating them is the single most-repeated failure in this routine.

live_window.note: 🔴 ADDED 2026-09-27 after Michael clicked three of the pass's best finds and two were graves. THE RULE: a posting has up to THREE INDEPENDENT TIME FACTS and the sweep must read all three before a row is reported as live. (1) POSTED — when it went up. (2) APPLICATION CLOSE — a stated deadline, OR a softer hiring-window phrase like 'interviews will take place in early September', which closes the door just as firmly. (3) ENGAGEMENT WINDOW — for freelance and limited-duration work, the dates the JOB ITSELF RUNS, often labelled `DURATION` on Playbill. ⚠ A row whose engagement window has already opened is usually already staffed; a row whose engagement window has CLOSED is dead regardless of how healthy its page looks.
live_window.the_two_corpses: Studio RRD Draftsperson — page renders in full with salary and apply-by-email intact, but `DURATION Aug 17, 2026 - Oct 9, 2026`, i.e. six weeks underway when it was reported to Michael as a top find. James & Jamesy Head Electrician / Lighting Programmer — page renders in full, but the body says 'ideally interviews will take place in early September 2026', three weeks shut. NEITHER was detectable by the URL gate, and neither had a conventional 'deadline' field to catch.
live_window.executor_rule: Capture and REPORT all three dates on every row. If the engagement window or hiring window has passed, the listing is NOTABLE prose, never a row. If you cannot determine them, say 'open status unconfirmed' — do NOT present it as live. 🚫 Never report a find to Michael as actionable on the strength of a resolving URL alone.
live_window.schema_owed: The 17-column schema has NO `close_date` and NO `last_verified`, so these facts currently have nowhere to live except prose inside `requirements`. This is the strongest evidence for the columns proposed in the 2026-09-25 schema review. ⚠ Schema changes are BUILD-SESSION ONLY (README rule 7) — do not add a column mid-pass.

Re-test a blocker before obeying it. 🔻 Lane seam, named not hidden: source discovery is Scout Sage's research lane per hooks/data-refresh.md; this was done by a research pass on Michael's explicit instruction. ⚠ CALIBRATION CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-27: the 09-26 focus pass returned 40 remote rows, five times the 3-8 band. The 3-8 band describes a VENUE-BOARD sweep. State which sweep produced a number before comparing it to the band.
